fatal_errors: The proposed intervention changes alloy composition and cooling rate rather than testing the effect of spark-plasma-sintering temperature on the same MgAlTiVFeCo powder.
The comparison cannot isolate the target processing mechanism because refractory-to-light ratio, elemental chemistry, density, segregation, and cooling history are changed together.
The cited evidence does not establish the proposed nanoscale intermetallic-cluster mechanism or its claimed corrosion benefit.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad lightweight-HEA objective and gives a testable composition–microstructure–property relationship. It also includes a controlled baseline, 3.5% NaCl corrosion testing, oxide mass gain, mechanical measurements, microscopy, and an explicit falsification rule. However, it does not reconstruct the central finding: SPS of initially BCC MgAlTiVFeCo powder at 1000 °C, producing 96.7% density, 1235.5 HV hardness, and uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases. It omits the 800–1000 °C sintering window, magnesium-volatilization upper boundary, 900 °C oxidation condition, specific AlV2O4/FeAl2O4/FeTiO3 phases, chloride-blocking passive-film mechanism, and biphasic parabolic oxidation kinetics. Its baseline is compositionally different rather than the same alloy sintered at 850–950 °C, and it does not require comparison of parabolic rate constants or corrosion-potential shifts. E1 supports the general link between segregation and protective oxide continuity, while E3 supports composition tuning for specific strength; neither directly supports nanoscale reinforcing clusters or improved NaCl corrosion, and E2 is only broad background. Thus, this is a scientifically plausible alternative rather than a reconstruction of the hidden target.
